chunks: Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said:
Concerning a man who is affected by janabah during travel, and he has with him only a small amount of water, fearing that if he performs ghusl he will become thirsty,
He said: 'If he fears thirst, then let him not pour out from it even a drop, and let him perform tayammum with the earth, for indeed the earth is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state of being on a journey
key_terms.بِالصَّعِيدِ: with clean earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.عَطَشًا: thirst that is feared as a harmful consequence
key_terms.قَطْرَةً: a single drop, emphasizing not wasting any water
key_terms.مَاءٌ قَلِيلٌ: a small amount of water insufficient to use without hardship
key_terms.وَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler in janabah do if he has too little water and fears thirst?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler in a state of janabah who has only a little water and fears thirst. In such a case, he should preserve the water and perform tayammum instead of ghusl, showing the priority of safeguarding life and necessity within ritual purity rulings.
